Court officers advised the group that was removed did not have any court related matters scheduled for today and were "all masked up". Upon heading back to the day's regular assignment, a radio call for a fight outside Roxbury Court broadcast by the B103D (Centeio/Mason) involving MA State Police. The Subject was yelling "Cuff me up!" during this encounter. Shortly after being placed in handcuffs, the Subject exclaimed that he couldn't breath. Officer Diaz did observe the Subject yelling this with full deep breaths, and reassured the Subject that his stomach was visibly rising and dropping several times indicating he was in fact taking breaths. The Officer and Trooper did reposition the Subject into a seated position to prevent any positional asphyxiation while awaiting a transport unit to arrive. At this time, the Subject laid straight back, and extended his legs forward while presenting what could have been signs of a seizure. Persons in the unruly crowd that had gathered and were filming the interaction began yelling that the Subject has a history of seizures. At this time dispatch was advised and an ambulance requested for the Subject/Prisoner. While awaiting the ambulance arrival, the Officer and Trooper did place the Subject into the recovery position on his left side, while a court officer stayed by the Subject's head, placing his hands underneath it to prevent any injury against the ground should he convulse again. The Officers did reassure the Subject that EMS was on the way. During this time, the Subject never lost consciousness, did not foam at the mouth, and his chest and belly were observed continually rising and falling in the same manner while the Subject breathed in and out uninterrupted. Officer Diaz did pull back the Subject's furry hood on his winter coat, and pulled down the "sheisty" ski mask that was covering his face, in order to provide an even more clear airway for him. Moments later, BFD Ladder04 and Boston EMS Ambulance 2A02 (Koo/Sullivan) responded. The Subject was placed on the stretcher and the handcuffs were repositioned to the side rails, one on each wrist. Officer Diaz conducted a more thorough search for weapons and contraband for rescuer safety, no items of concern were found. MSP then escorted the Subject to the Boston Medical Center. At about 7:11 p.m. on Tuesday, September 2, 2025, while working the front desk at Boston Police Department District D-14 (Brighton/ Allston neighborhoods) XXXWashington Street, Brighton Officer Coleman was approached by an unknown male individual who requested assistance in locating his 78-year-old father. The male reported that his father had been gone for approximately two hours while driving his Subaru to pick up an unknown party. The male further stated that his father did not have his cellular phone with him. The individual expressed interest in having Boston Police compel Subaru to provide the real-time GPS coordinates of the vehicle. The unknown individual indicated concern for his father’s location, but emphasized law enforcement obtaining GPS data over filing a missing person’s report. Officer Coleman conferred with Sgt. Murphy, who directed him to the Detectives Unit. Officer Coleman, then, spoke with Detective O’Connor, who advised Officer Coleman there was not sufficient legal basis for law enforcement to compel Subaru to provide GPS coordinates. Additionally, Officer Coleman consulted with Sgt. Det. Martin Joseph regarding the matter who requested this report to be completed. Officer Coleman returned to inform the individual that if he was genuinely concerned for his father’s safety, the appropriate step would be to contact 911 and request that an officer respond to the residence where his father was last seen, in accordance with Rule 317 and Department practice: the initial responding officer should be dispatched to, or respond to, the location where the missing person was last observed. The individual stated that he believed his father was “probably lost, not missing,” and reiterated his interest in law enforcement forcing Subaru to disclose GPS data. I advised him that GPS tracking is considered a search under United States v. Jones, 565 U.S. 400 (2012) and Carpenter v. United States, 585 U.S. ___ (2018), and that compelling Subaru to release such data without a warrant or court order would constitute a violation of the Fourth Amendment. I explained that lawful process supported by probable cause is required and that the circumstances presented his father not carrying his phone did not rise to the level of exigency. The individual then inquired what would happen if he reported the vehicle stolen. I advised him that filing a false report of a crime for the purpose of obtaining GPS data would constitute a violation of M.G.L. c. 268, § 39 and could result in criminal charges. Officer Coleman further advised the unknown individual of alternative lawful options, including the availability of aftermarket GPS tracking devices. Officer Coleman advised unknown individual to reconsider the limitations of subscribing to a GPS service that does not provide immediate consumer access. The individual was provided with the contact number for the Boston Police Dispatch Call Center +1 (617) 343-4911 should he change his mind and wish to file a missing person’s report. The unknown individual had not called to file a missing person report since this report was completed at the end of Officer Coleman's shift.
